title: Async path stall — containment and deferred recompile plan
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
During a staged rollout of an asynchronous background kernel recompile optimization, we observed repeated 'async path stall' incidents that caused elevated p95/p99 token latencies for multi-turn chat workloads. The symptom was a sudden rise in tail latency on nodes performing deferred recompiles: worker threads entered a stall state while waiting for kernel candidate metadata to become available, causing request queues to pile up and cascade across the scheduler. Impacted customers experienced increased completion latency and degraded throughput for ~12–45 minutes depending on autoscale reaction and canary routing heuristics.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-09 22:14 UTC: Rollout of deferred recompile across ~30% of canary pool (controlled feature flag).
- 2026-03-09 22:27 UTC: First alerts: runtime p95 increased for chat-rt route.
- 2026-03-09 22:32 UTC: Ops mitigated by draining flagged nodes and re-routing to compatible fallback model variant.
- 2026-03-09 22:40–23:00 UTC: Multiple recovery cycles; nodes re-entered degraded state after background recompile resumed.
- 2026-03-10 00:05 UTC: Emergency rollback of deferred recompile feature flag.

Root cause hypothesis (summary):
A combination of three factors created a stall mode: (1) background kernel recompile uses a single-flight metadata population mechanism that can block serving threads when there is a contention spike; (2) the scheduler's prefetch heuristic prioritizes filling GPU batches and delays eviction of requests waiting on metadata, amplifying queue depth; and (3) some kernel candidates require on-the-fly micro-kernel generation that briefly holds locks while compiling artifacts into shared memory. Under a bursty arrival pattern (chat turn bursts + long-prefix KV cache misses), these locks align and produce a head-of-line stall that propagates via autoscaler and routing hysteresis.

Why this escaped pre-rollout detection:
- Synthetic microbenchmarks used steady-state input distributions and did not emulate chat-burst arrival patterns with concurrent KV cache churn.
- Canary traffic fraction and canary selection did not exercise heterogeneous model-variant mixes that trigger candidate compilations.
- Observability gaps: no focused metric for "metadata populate blocking time" and limited stack traces for blocked worker threads in production.

Containment steps completed during incident:
1) Immediate rollback of deferred recompile flag across canary nodes.
2) Emergency scheduler update to enforce an upper bound on wait-on-metadata per-request (temporary 200ms soft-limit) to force fallbacks to precompiled kernel variants.
3) Reroute policy changed to avoid draining nodes performing background compilation until compile tasks complete, reducing oscillation.
4) Post-incident auto-remediation: added a soft circuit-breaker that rejects background compile scheduling if the node's request queue exceeds 50% of the serving capacity.

Planned long-term mitigations (this ticket):
A. Single-flight non-blocking metadata populate: refactor populate path to use wait-free futures and short-circuit serving threads; background compile should populate metadata only into ephemeral per-worker caches before promoting to shared cache under low-load conditions.
B. Deferred recompile scheduler: implement a background recompile scheduler that enforces rate limits, backoff, and a compile window based on node utilization and request arrival variance.
C. Compile isolation sandbox: run micro-kernel emitters in isolated worker threads/processes with bounded CPU and memory; use copy-on-write shared memory promotion to avoid holding global locks.
D. Observability and SLOs: introduce new metrics (metadata_populate_block_ms, compile_queue_length, compile_failure_rate), a stacked-stacktrace capture for blocked threads, and an alert that fires at 50ms median blocked time.
E. Canary harness expansion: extend canary traffic generator to include chat-burst synthetic workloads, KV cache churn scenarios, and mixed model-variant routing (explicitly trigger on-the-fly kernel generation paths).
F. Scheduler hard guard: add a request-level timeout for waiting on metadata; requests exceeding threshold should be fast-failed to fallback variant or proxy route with a controlled degradation path.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- A1: Implement non-blocking metadata populate prototype and microbench (owner: Carlos Ortega) — due 2026-03-18.
- A2: Build deferred recompile scheduler with rate limiting/backoff and unit tests (owner: Priya Nair) — due 2026-03-25.
- A3: Add compile isolation sandbox and promote shared cache via promotion window (owner: Dario Petrov) — due 2026-04-01.
- A4: Add metrics and stacktrace capture, and wire new alerts to Slack/Pager (owner: Maya Chen) — due 2026-03-16.
- A5: Expand canary harness scenarios and add rollover test to CI (owner: QE Team — contact: Lena Park) — due 2026-03-22.
- A6: Update scheduler to enforce temporary wait-on-metadata soft-limits and integrate fallback flows (owner: Carlos Ortega) — due 2026-03-14 (critical hotfix).
- A7: Postmortem writeup and customer comms template (owner: Emily Blake) — due 2026-03-15.

2026-03-12 — Dario: Sandbox approach validated in staging: compiling micro-kernel in separate process avoids worker thread blocking; minor IPC perf overhead observed but acceptable.
2026-03-13 — QE (Lena): Canary harness updated and added burst profile tests; running overnight to collect variance data.
2026-03-14 — Ops: Deployed temporary scheduler soft-limit (200ms) to prod canaries; no customer-facing incidents since deployment.
updates: 2026-03-13 — A6 hotfix merged and rolled to 50% of canary nodes: PR #8341. Monitoring dashboard linked.
